ai.description: *Calotes minor* is a small agamid reaching 25 cm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark nuchal crest and a white or yellow stripe along the flanks. A dark patch typically marks the shoulder.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes minor* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, deep black patch on each side of the neck, which is absent in other similar Indian *Calotes* species.
ai.habitat: *Calotes minor* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands across the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Calotes minor* is primarily diurnal, often remaining motionless on tree trunks or branches to ambush small insects while blending into its surroundings with cryptic coloration.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes minor* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–11 eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes minor* is found across northern and central India, extending into Pakistan and Nepal, typically inhabiting scrublands and forests up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
